provider: Solana public RPC (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com / api.mainnet.solana.com), keyless alternatives (publicnode), and Helius (RPC, LaserStream WSS, DAS, Enhanced Transactions [legacy], Parsed Events, Parsed Streams, getTransactionsForAddress, Wallet API, Webhooks)
summary:
Status on 2026-09-28, live-tested from Europe (RPC node fra286, solana-core 4.3.0).

(1) Solana public mainnet RPC. It works server-side with no key and 50-80 ms warm latency (200-275 ms on the first TLS request). It is not usable from a browser: any request that carries an Origin header, which every browser sends, gets HTTP 403 {"code":403,"message":"Access forbidden"}. That applies to both HTTP POST and the WebSocket upgrade. The CORS preflight returns 200 but still fails. Per-IP per-method limits are tiny: getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction and getTokenAccountsByOwner allow 10 calls per 10 s, getMultipleAccounts 50, getBalance and getTokenSupply 150. getTokenLargestAccounts has method-limit 0, so it always returns 429. Solana's docs say the endpoint is not for production and that high-traffic sites may be blocked. The public WebSocket is fine for a server-side process: logsSubscribe on pump.fun delivered about 240-260 notifications/s (about 0.46 MB/s, 1.87 KB average, roughly 70% failed bot transactions). Vercel serverless cannot hold such a socket.

(2) solana-rpc.publicnode.com is the only keyless endpoint that worked from a browser (CORS *, HTTP and WS). It blocks "indexed" methods: getTokenSupply, getTokenAccountsByOwner and getProgramAccounts need a personal token, and getTokenLargestAccounts is blocked. Its WS delivered only about 40-45% of the notifications the official WS did. drpc, ankr, onfinality and blockeden are all unusable without a key.

(3) Transaction v1 (SIMD-0385) has been live on mainnet since 2026-09-15. Every getTransaction, getBlock, getTransactionsForAddress or transactionSubscribe(full) call must send maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 1, or it fails with error -32015. I saw this live: 2 of the pump.fun trades I sampled were v1. JS SDKs must be @solana/kit 8.0 or later, or @solana/web3.js v3.

(4) Helius. Documentation only; no key was available. Every Helius host (mainnet., beta., api-mainnet., api.helius.xyz) answers 401 with ACAO * when called without a key. Free plan: 1M credits/month, 10 RPC req/s, 2 DAS or Enhanced req/s, 1 sendTransaction/s, 5 LaserStream-WSS connections per project (standard subscribe methods only), 5 webhooks, 5 Parsed Streams connections. Developer ($49): 10M credits, 50 rps, DAS 10 rps, plus the transactionSubscribe and enhanced accountSubscribe WS extensions, and 150 WS connections. LaserStream gRPC on mainnet needs Business ($499), and gRPC cannot run on Vercel serverless.
- Credit costs. Standard RPC is 1 credit per call. DAS is 10 per call. Enhanced Transactions is 100 per call and is in legacy maintenance mode. Its successor, Parsed Events, is 10 per request and is available on all plans (metered since 2026-09-24). getTransactionsForAddress is 10 credits per 100 full transactions returned, or 10 credits flat for signatures only. Webhooks are 1 credit per event. Parsed Streams are 1 credit per event. All WebSocket data costs 2 credits per 0.1 MB plus 1 credit per connection.
- A browser-exposed key can be restricted with the dashboard "RPC Access Control Rules": Allowed Domains, IPs or CIDRs. There is also a masked "Secure URL" (5 req/s per IP), but only on paid plans.
- Headline limitation for ORBYT: WS data is metered, and Free allows only 5 concurrent WS connections per project. One pump.fun logsSubscribe firehose is about 33k credits/hour. So a live trade feed per browser user cannot run on Helius Free. Use Parsed Streams for low-volume events (creates, migrations), webhooks to a Vercel route for tracked wallets, and HTTP polling or server fan-out for trades.
auth:
Public RPC: none. Blocked when an Origin header is present, so server-side only.
publicnode: none for basic methods. "Indexed" methods need a personal token from allnodes.com/publicnode.
Helius: API key as the query parameter ?api-key=KEY on every host, i.e. https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY, wss://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY, https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/v1/parsed-events/...?api-key=KEY, https://api.helius.xyz/v1/wallet/...?api-key=KEY. Keyless calls return 401 "Unauthorized". The WS upgrade without a key returns 401 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32401,"message":"missing api key"}}.

Helius free tier: 1M credits/month, RPC 10 req/s, DAS/Enhanced/Wallet API 2 req/s, sendTransaction 1/s, getProgramAccounts 5/s, 5 webhooks (100k addresses each), LaserStream WSS standard methods with 5 concurrent connections per project across all its keys (1,000 subscriptions per connection), Parsed Streams 5 connections × 25 subscriptions, Parsed Events included, Wallet API included. Not on Free: transactionSubscribe and enhanced accountSubscribe (Developer+), LaserStream gRPC mainnet (Business+), Secure URL (paid only), getTransfersByAddress (Developer+).

Key protection (docs: /docs/rpc/protect-your-keys): the dashboard "RPC Access Control Rules" support Allowed Domains (e.g. orbytai.org, www.orbytai.org), Allowed IPs and Allowed CIDRs (public IPs only). Alternatives are a masked Secure URL (https://<id>-fast-mainnet.helius-rpc.com, 5 req/s per IP, paid plans only) or your own proxy.

Suggested env vars:
- Server only: HELIUS_API_KEY; HELIUS_RPC_URL=https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=... (or https://beta.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=..., the Gatekeeper host with lower latency and the same key); HELIUS_API_BASE=https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com (for /v1/parsed-events and legacy /v0); HELIUS_WALLET_API_BASE=https://api.helius.xyz; HELIUS_WEBHOOK_AUTH_HEADER (the secret you set as authHeader and check in the Vercel route); SOLANA_PUBLIC_RPC_URL=https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com (fallback only).
- Browser: NEXT_PUBLIC_HELIUS_WS_URL=wss://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=<separate key, domain-restricted, low credit budget>; optional NEXT_PUBLIC_HELIUS_SECURE_RPC_URL (paid plans); NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLANA_WS_FALLBACK_URL=wss://solana-rpc.publicnode.com.
- Never expose the main HELIUS_API_KEY with a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.
base_urls: https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com (JSON-RPC POST; alias https://api.mainnet.solana.com is what solana.com/docs/references/clusters now lists; both returned solana-core 4.3.0)
https://solana-rpc.publicnode.com and wss://solana-rpc.publicnode.com (keyless, CORS *, restricted methods)
https://beta.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY (Helius Gatekeeper edge: same methods/keys/pricing, lower latency; also the only host for Parsed Streams/preprocessedSubscribe/preconfSubscribe)
wss://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY (LaserStream WebSocket: standard subscriptions + Helius extensions)
wss://beta.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY (LaserStream WSS via Gatekeeper + Parsed Streams parsedTransactionSubscribe)

https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/v0/transactions and /v0/addresses/{address}/transactions?api-key=KEY (Enhanced Transactions, legacy; current docs use mainnet.helius-rpc.com; api-mainnet.helius-rpc.com and api.helius.xyz still resolve and return 401 keyless)
https://api.helius.xyz/v0/webhooks?api-key=KEY (webhook management; OpenAPI servers also list mainnet.helius-rpc.com)
cors:
Tested with the header "Origin: https://www.orbytai.org".

api.mainnet-beta.solana.com and api.mainnet.solana.com: the OPTIONS preflight returns 200 and echoes access-control-allow-origin: https://www.orbytai.org. However, the actual POST with an Origin header returns HTTP 403 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code": 403,"message":"Access forbidden"}} with ACAO *. The same happened with Origin http://localhost:3000, and the WebSocket upgrade with an Origin also gets 403 (a Node client sending an Origin got close code 1006). Without an Origin header the response is 200, and the header reads the literal string "access-control-allow-origin: backend_traffic". So a browser cannot call it: server-side or proxy only.

solana-rpc.publicnode.com: the preflight returns 204 with ACAO *, POST responses carry ACAO *, and the WS accepts a browser Origin. Browser-callable, but getTokenSupply, getTokenAccountsByOwner and getProgramAccounts return 403 "Indexed requests require a personal token", and getTokenLargestAccounts returns 403 "Request blocked".

Helius (all hosts: mainnet.helius-rpc.com, beta.helius-rpc.com, api-mainnet.helius-rpc.com, api.helius.xyz): the preflight returns 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Allow-Headers: *, Authorization, and Allow-Methods: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, OPTIONS. 401 responses also carry ACAO *. So a browser can call Helius directly; the only gate is the api-key, which should be restricted with Allowed Domains (DOCUMENTED). Remember that non-browser clients can spoof Origin.

Others: drpc (ACAO *, but "chain is not available on free plan"), ankr (403, API key required), onfinality public (429, 1 req/s), blockeden (401).
rate_limits:
Solana public mainnet, live headers on every response: x-ratelimit-tier: free; x-ratelimit-rps-limit: 250; x-ratelimit-conn-limit: 40; x-ratelimit-connrate-limit: 40; x-ratelimit-pubsub-limit: 10; x-ratelimit-endpoint-limit: unlimited. Per-method x-ratelimit-method-limit per IP per 10 s window:
- getHealth, getVersion, getBalance, getTokenSupply: 150
- getMultipleAccounts: 50
- getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction, getTokenAccountsByOwner: 10. A burst test on getSignaturesForAddress gave 10 × 200, then 429 {"code":429,"message":"Too many requests for a specific RPC call"} with retry-after: 10.
- getTokenLargestAccounts: 0, i.e. always 429.

Official docs (solana.com/docs/references/clusters): 100 requests per 10 s per IP; 40 per 10 s per IP for a single RPC method; 40 concurrent connections per IP; 40 new connections per 10 s per IP; 100 MB of data per 30 s. The docs add "not intended for production" and "high-traffic websites may be blocked without prior notice". No 429s occurred at about 3 req/s except on the blocked method and the deliberate burst. Vercel functions share egress IPs, so expect worse.

publicnode: no rate-limit headers; 115-330 ms.

Helius, per second: RPC Free 10 / Dev 50 / Business 200 / Pro 500. DAS and Enhanced (and Wallet API): 2 / 10 / 50 / 100. sendTransaction: 1 / 5 / 50 / 100. getProgramAccounts: 5 / 25 / 50 / 75. Sender: 50/s on all plans.
- Batch limits: getTransaction up to 100 items per JSON-RPC batch; other historical methods 10 per batch; getTransactionsForAddress and getTransfersByAddress allow no batching.
- LaserStream WSS: 5 / 150 / 250 / 1,000 concurrent connections, 1,000 subscriptions per connection, 10-minute inactivity timeout (ping every 30-60 s).
- Parsed Streams: 5 / 10 / 50 / 50 connections × 25 subscriptions.
- Webhooks: 5 / 50 / 50 / 50, 100k addresses each.
- On 429/5xx: backoff starting at 1 s, doubling to a 30 s max, ±25% jitter, 5 attempts.
- Credits: RPC 1; getProgramAccounts 10 (V2 paginated 1); DAS 10; Enhanced Transactions 100; Parsed Events 10 per request; getTransactionsForAddress 10 per 100 full transactions (10 minimum) or 10 flat for signatures; Wallet API balances/history 100; webhooks 1 per event (management 100); Parsed Streams 1 per event; WSS and gRPC 2 credits per 0.1 MB plus 1 credit per connection; preprocessedSubscribe 0.1 per message (paid plans).
- Measured on the public WS: a pump.fun logsSubscribe is about 0.464 MB/s, which on Helius would be about 33,400 credits per hour per subscription (the Free plan's 1M/month is gone in about 30 hours).

endpoints.name: getTokenSupply (public RPC)
endpoints.purpose: Total supply and decimals for market cap / FDV (works for SPL and Token-2022).
endpoints.response_shape: result.context.slot (int), result.context.apiVersion ('4.3.0'); result.value.amount (STRING, raw base units; BONK = "8799437915923265810" which is above 2^53, so use BigInt), result.value.decimals (int; BONK 5, pump.fun 6), result.value.uiAmount (float, LOSSY), result.value.uiAmountString (exact decimal string). pump.fun mints have supply 1000000000000000 raw = 1,000,000,000 tokens.
endpoints.params_limits: one mint per call; method limit 150/10s/IP

endpoints.name: getTokenLargestAccounts (public RPC / publicnode)
endpoints.purpose: Top-20 holders (token ACCOUNTS, not wallets).
endpoints.response_shape: Live on public mainnet: HTTP 429 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":429,"message":"Too many requests for a specific RPC call"}} with header x-ratelimit-method-limit: 0 and retry-after: 10, even for the FIRST call (method disabled). publicnode: HTTP 403 {"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Request blocked"}}. Documented success shape (works on Helius, 1 credit): result.value[] (max 20) {address (token-account pubkey), amount (raw string), decimals, uiAmount, uiAmountString}. You must resolve each account's owner (getMultipleAccounts jsonParsed -> parsed.info.owner) to show wallets. The #1 account is usually the bonding-curve/pool vault.
endpoints.params_limits: top 20 only

endpoints.name: getSignaturesForAddress (public RPC)
endpoints.purpose: Recent activity on a pool/bonding-curve/wallet (trade feed seed, wallet history paging).
endpoints.response_shape: result[] newest-first: {signature (base58), slot (int), blockTime (int UNIX SECONDS, nullable), err (null or e.g. {"InstructionError":[1,{"Custom":13}]}), memo (null|string), confirmationStatus ('processed'|'confirmed'|'finalized'), transactionIndex (int, position in block)}. Includes FAILED txs: all 5 latest signatures of the pump.fun program were failed bot txs, so filter err==null. Only txs where the address is in accountKeys; a wallet's ATA-only activity is NOT included.
endpoints.params_limits: limit 1-1000 (default 1000); paginate with before=<last signature>; method limit 10 per 10s per IP (burst-verified)

endpoints.name: getTransaction jsonParsed (public RPC) + swap derivation
endpoints.purpose: Decode a real swap (trade feed row, wallet PnL fills). Six real swap fixtures saved: pump.fun bonding-curve buyExactSolIn (legacy), BuyV2 (v0), Sell (v1), PumpSwap sell (Token-2022, v0), PumpSwap dust buy (legacy), and an aggregator buy paid in USDC with a relayer fee payer.
endpoints.response_shape:
result.slot; result.blockTime (UNIX s); result.version ('legacy' | 0 | 1); result.transactionIndex; result.transaction.signatures[0]; result.transaction.message.accountKeys[] {pubkey, signer, writable, source ('transaction'|'lookupTable')} (jsonParsed already merges address-lookup-table keys); message.instructions[] (parsed or {programId, accounts[], data}); message.recentBlockhash; message.addressTableLookups (v0 only); message.transactionConfig (v1 only: {computeUnitLimit, heapSize, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit, priorityFee = TOTAL lamports}, and no ComputeBudget instructions). result.meta: err, status {Ok:null}, fee (lamports, charged to accountKeys[0]), preBalances[] / postBalances[] (lamports, index-aligned with accountKeys), preTokenBalances[] / postTokenBalances[] {accountIndex, mint, owner (wallet or PDA that owns the token account), programId (Tokenkeg... or Tokenz...2022), uiTokenAmount {amount (raw string), decimals, uiAmount, uiAmountString}}, innerInstructions[], logMessages[] (pump.fun TradeEvent appears as 'Program data: vdt/007mYe...'), computeUnitsConsumed, costUnits, rewards.

SWAP DERIVATION (implemented and verified in tmp/rpc-helius/derive.mjs):
(1) Pick the trader: the signer whose token balances changed. It is usually accountKeys[0], but relayer/fee-payer txs exist, e.g. the aggregator fixture where the trader is signer #2.
(2) Token deltas: for each (owner, mint), Δ = Σ post.amount − Σ pre.amount using BigInt. A token account missing from pre (created in the tx) counts as 0; one missing from post (closed) counts as 0.
(3) Native SOL: Δlamports = postBalances[i] − preBalances[i] for the trader's index. Add meta.fee back if the trader is accountKeys[0].
(4) Add back rent moved into or out of token accounts OWNED by the trader (ATA create/close), because it is not trade value. For those accounts, subtract their WSOL token delta so it isn't double-counted.
(5) WSOL: add the trader's So111...112 token delta to the SOL side. Wrap/unwrap accounts created and closed inside the same tx never appear in token balances (PumpSwap fixture), so their SOL appears only in pre/postBalances of the trader.
(6) Result: side = BUY if the single non-WSOL mint delta > 0, else SELL. Price in SOL/token = |ΔSOL| / (|Δtoken| / 10^decimals). This includes protocol, creator and bot fees; the pool-side delta or the pump TradeEvent gives the pre-fee price.
(7) Token-2022 is handled identically. Use per-owner deltas, not transfer amounts, because transfer-fee extensions make sent ≠ received.
(8) If the quote is USDC or another token, you get two mint deltas (the aggregator fixture: +119461.597043 BfK1...pump, −9.827851 USDC) and must convert via a USD/SOL price.

Verified outputs: PumpSwap sell = +2.584865588 SOL for −290247.583767 tokens; pump.fun buyExactSolIn = −0.004005 SOL (after adding back fee 6000 and ATA rent 2,039,280) for +4,833,319.952665 tokens; the v1 sell = +1.96599817 SOL. A trading-bot program took its own ~1% fee, so net SOL is less than the curve's sol_amount minus pump fees.
endpoints.params_limits: one signature per call (JSON-RPC batch arrays exist, but each item counts toward the 10/10s per-IP method limit). Omitting maxSupportedTransactionVersion or setting it to 0 gives error -32015 on v1 txs (live).
endpoints.freshness: available about 1 s after confirmation at commitment confirmed; responses are 11-60 KB

endpoints.name: getBalance (public RPC)
endpoints.purpose: Wallet SOL balance (portfolio, wallet tracker).
endpoints.response_shape: result.context.{slot, apiVersion}; result.value = lamports (int; 9759034646 = 9.759 SOL).

endpoints.name: getTokenAccountsByOwner jsonParsed (public RPC) for SPL Token and Token-2022
endpoints.purpose: Wallet token holdings (portfolio); two calls needed because the filter takes one programId (or {mint}).
endpoints.response_shape: result.value[] {pubkey (token account), account {lamports (rent: 2039280 for older 165-byte accounts, 1513840 for new 170-byte Token-2022 accounts), owner (token program id), space (165 SPL / 170 Token-2022 with immutableOwner), executable, rentEpoch (u64 max 18446744073709552000, lossy in JS), data {program ('spl-token'|'spl-token-2022'), space, parsed {type:'account', info {mint, owner (wallet), isNative, state ('initialized'|'frozen'), tokenAmount {amount (raw string), decimals, uiAmount, uiAmountString}, extensions?[] e.g. {extension:'immutableOwner'}}}}}}. Includes ZERO-balance accounts: the tested wallet had 18 Token-2022 and 6 SPL accounts, most at 0, so filter amount !== '0'. No prices and no metadata.
endpoints.params_limits: 10/10s/IP; no pagination

endpoints.name: getMultipleAccounts (public RPC; also works on publicnode from the browser)
endpoints.purpose: Batch-read mints (on-chain Token-2022 name/symbol/uri), token accounts, and pump.fun bonding-curve state (price, market cap, graduation progress for Final Stretch).
endpoints.response_shape:
result.value[] aligned with the request order (null if missing).
- Token-2022 mint: data.parsed.info {decimals, supply (raw string), mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, isInitialized, extensions[] incl. {extension:'metadataPointer', state{metadataAddress}}, {extension:'tokenMetadata', state{name, symbol, uri (IPFS JSON), updateAuthority, additionalMetadata[]}}}; data.program 'spl-token-2022'; space 426. pump.fun Token-2022 mints carry name/symbol/uri on-chain, so no Metaplex lookup is needed.
- Program-owned accounts fall back to data = [base64, 'base64'].
- pump.fun bonding curve layout (151 bytes, verified): 8-byte discriminator 17b7f83760d8ac60 | u64 virtual_token_reserves | u64 virtual_sol_reserves (lamports) | u64 real_token_reserves | u64 real_sol_reserves | u64 token_total_supply | bool complete | pubkey creator | ... Price in SOL/token = (vSol/1e9) / (vTok/1e6). Market cap in SOL = price × 1e9. Progress = 1 − real_token_reserves / 793,100,000e6. Live example: 17.605 SOL real, 50.03% progress, market cap 70.4 SOL.
endpoints.params_limits: max 100 pubkeys per call; 50/10s/IP on public mainnet

endpoints.name: getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption (public RPC)
endpoints.purpose: Know the current rent constants so ATA create/close lamports aren't counted as trade value.
endpoints.response_shape: result = 1488440 (lamports for 165 bytes). Rent was lowered: it used to be 2039280, which still appears on older accounts and on some txs that over-fund. Never hardcode 2039280.

endpoints.name: Public RPC browser-origin rejection
endpoints.request: POST https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com with header Origin: https://www.orbytai.org
endpoints.purpose: Proves the public endpoint cannot serve a browser (HTTP and WS).
endpoints.response_shape: HTTP 403 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":403,"message":"Access forbidden"},"id":1}; all x-ratelimit-* headers empty; ACAO *. The WS upgrade with an Origin also gets 403.

endpoints.name: publicnode keyless HTTP RPC
endpoints.purpose: Only keyless RPC usable directly from the browser: account/tx reads.
endpoints.response_shape: Standard Solana JSON-RPC (apiVersion 4.2.2). OK methods: getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction (maxSupportedTransactionVersion 1), getBalance, getMultipleAccounts. Blocked with 403 {"code":-32602,"message":"Indexed requests require a personal token. Get one at: https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode"}: getTokenSupply, getTokenAccountsByOwner, getProgramAccounts. getTokenLargestAccounts gets 403 'Request blocked'. 115-330 ms; one 403 took 3.1 s.
endpoints.auth: none (personal token needed for indexed methods)
endpoints.params_limits: no rate-limit headers; limits undisclosed

endpoints.name: Helius RPC (standard Solana JSON-RPC, incl. getTokenLargestAccounts and getProgramAccountsV2)
endpoints.request: POST https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY (or https://beta.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=KEY) with a standard JSON-RPC body
endpoints.purpose: Production replacement for the public RPC: all reads above without the per-method throttles.
endpoints.response_shape: Identical to Solana JSON-RPC. Keyless live check: HTTP 401 body 'Unauthorized', ACAO *.
endpoints.params_limits: Free 10 rps / Dev 50 / Biz 200 / Pro 500; getProgramAccounts 5/25/50/75 per s; getTransaction batch ≤100; 1 credit per call (getProgramAccounts 10, V2 1)
endpoints.freshness: real-time; Gatekeeper beta host lower latency

endpoints.name: Helius getTransactionsForAddress (Helius-exclusive RPC method)
endpoints.purpose: Wallet analytics/PnL backfill (full txs including ATA activity, succeeded-only, oldest-first), token launch analysis (first buyers), pool trade-history backfill.
endpoints.response_shape: result.data[]: in signatures mode {signature, slot, transactionIndex, err, memo, blockTime (s), confirmationStatus}; in full mode each item = a getTransaction-shaped object {slot, blockTime, transaction, meta, ...}. result.paginationToken 'slot:position' (absent at the end).
endpoints.auth: ?api-key=; no plan restriction stated (getTransfersByAddress IS Developer+)
endpoints.params_limits: limit up to 1000 in both modes; no JSON-RPC batching; processed commitment not supported; tokenAccounts filters rely on the token-balance owner field (post slot 111,491,819, about Dec 2022); mainnet retention unlimited

endpoints.name: Helius Enhanced Transactions: parse signatures (LEGACY, maintenance mode)
endpoints.request: POST https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/v0/transactions?api-key=KEY body {"transactions":["<sig>",...],"commitment":"confirmed"} (older hosts api-mainnet.helius-rpc.com and api.helius.xyz also answer 401 keyless)
endpoints.purpose: Human-readable parsed txs incl. events.swap. Superseded by Parsed Events.
endpoints.params_limits: ≤100 signatures per request; 100 credits per call; DAS/Enhanced rate 2 rps on Free

endpoints.name: Helius Enhanced Transactions: address history (LEGACY)
endpoints.purpose: Parsed wallet/pool history filtered by type (legacy).
endpoints.response_shape: Array of EnhancedTransaction (same as above). With a type filter the server searches at runtime and may return {"error":"Failed to find events within the search period. To continue search, query the API again with the `before-signature` parameter set to <sig>."}, which you then continue from. The param is now 'before-signature'; old 'before' is not in the current spec.
endpoints.params_limits: limit 1-100 (default 10); 100 credits per call

endpoints.name: Helius Parsed Events: parse transactions (successor to Enhanced)
endpoints.purpose: IDL-decoded txs (3,600+ programs) with swap summary: trade feed enrichment and wallet activity labels.
endpoints.response_shape:
Array in input order of {signature, parserStatus ('OK'|'ERROR'), parsed | parserError {code, message}, rawTransaction?}.
parsed = {slot, blockTime (s|null), fee (lamports), feePayer, transactionStatus ('OK'|'ERROR'), error?, decodedError? {instructionIndex, programId, programName, code, name, msg}, nativeTransfers[] {fromUserAccount, toUserAccount, amount (lamports)}, tokenTransfers[] {fromUserAccount, toUserAccount, fromTokenAccount, toTokenAccount, rawTokenAmount (RAW number, divide by 10^decimals), decimals, tokenStandard, mint}, summary {type ('swap'|'transfer'|'add_liquidity'|'remove_liquidity'|'create_account'|'create_token_account'), description, parsedData} | null, instructions[] {instructionIndex, innerInstructionIndex, stackHeight, programId, rawAccounts[], rawData, summary, programName, instructionName, decoded {args (snake_case; u64 as strings), accounts[] {name, pubkey, isSigner, isWritable}} | null}}.
Swap parsedData example (Jupiter): {type:'swap', protocol:'jupiter', kind:'swap', in_amount (raw string), actual_out_amount (raw string), input_mint, output_mint, inner_swaps[] {amm_program_id, amm_program_name, input_amount, output_amount, input_mint, output_mint}}. The shape varies by protocol.
endpoints.params_limits: 10 credits per request (metered from 2026-09-24; earlier users not charged until 2026-10-01); max signatures per request not stated in the spec (the old endpoint allowed 100); shares the DAS/Enhanced 2 rps Free limit

endpoints.name: Helius Parsed Events: transaction history
endpoints.purpose: Parsed wallet history for the wallet tracker/analytics. There is no server-side type filter: filter client-side on parsed.summary.type==='swap'.
endpoints.response_shape: {data: TransactionResult[] (same as the parse endpoint), paginationToken: 'slot:index' (missing = end)}
endpoints.params_limits: limit 1-100 (default 100); 10 credits per request

endpoints.name: Helius DAS getAsset (showFungible)
endpoints.purpose: Token metadata (name, symbol, image, token_program, Token-2022 mint_extensions) and a cached USD price for verified tokens.
endpoints.response_shape: result.id; result.interface ('FungibleToken'|'FungibleAsset'|...); result.content {json_uri, metadata {name, symbol, description, token_standard}, links {image}, files[]}; result.token_info {symbol, supply (raw int), decimals, token_program, price_info {price_per_token (float), total_price, currency 'USDC'}, balance?, associated_token_address?}; result.mint_extensions {transfer_fee_config, metadata, ...}; authorities[], ownership, mutable, burnt. Market cap = supply/10^decimals × price_per_token.
endpoints.params_limits: 10 credits; Free 2 rps
endpoints.freshness: price_info cached up to 600 s and only for verified tokens, so it is NOT suitable for live prices or new pump.fun tokens

endpoints.name: Helius DAS getAssetBatch
endpoints.purpose: Bulk metadata for Discover rows / wallet holdings.
endpoints.response_shape: result[] of getAsset objects (null for unknown ids), in request order.
endpoints.params_limits: up to 1,000 ids per call; 10 credits per call

endpoints.name: Helius DAS getTokenAccounts (holders by mint)
endpoints.purpose: Holder list/count for a mint (paginate all pages); wallet token accounts by owner.
endpoints.response_shape: result {total (count IN THIS PAGE, not the global count), limit, page | cursor, token_accounts[] {address, mint, owner, amount (raw int), delegated_amount, frozen}}. Holder count = number of distinct owners with amount>0 across all pages. Exclude bonding-curve/pool vault owners.
endpoints.params_limits: limit ≤1000; page-based or cursor (keyset) pagination; 10 credits per page, so a 50k-holder token costs about 500 credits per full count

endpoints.name: Helius DAS getAssetsByOwner (portfolio)
endpoints.purpose: One-call wallet portfolio (SPL + Token-2022 + NFTs + SOL) with USD values for verified tokens.
endpoints.response_shape: result {total, limit, page, items[] (getAsset shape incl. token_info {balance (raw), decimals, supply, token_program, associated_token_address, price_info {price_per_token, total_price, currency}}), nativeBalance {lamports, price_per_sol, total_price} (when showNativeBalance), grand_total? }. searchAssets with tokenType:'fungible' is the alternative.
endpoints.params_limits: limit ≤1000 per page; 10 credits per call
endpoints.freshness: prices ≤600 s cache, verified tokens only

endpoints.name: Helius Wallet API (beta)
endpoints.purpose: Wallet tracker convenience: identity labels, funding source, balance changes per tx.
endpoints.response_shape: balances: tokens (100 per page) with pricePerToken, usdValue (nullable, hourly estimates), totalUsdValue (current page only); history: items with balanceChanges[]. See OpenAPI openapi/wallet-api/openapi.yaml.
endpoints.params_limits: 100 credits per request for balances/history; 2 rps Free

endpoints.name: Helius Webhooks
endpoints.purpose: Serverless-friendly push: Helius POSTs txs for tracked wallets/pools to a Vercel route (wallet tracker alerts, trade ingestion into a DB).
endpoints.response_shape: raw webhook payload = array of getTransaction-shaped objects (apply the same swap derivation); enhanced = EnhancedTransaction array (legacy parser). Verify the Authorization header equals authHeader.
endpoints.params_limits: Free 5 webhooks; ≤100k addresses per webhook (the dashboard UI allows 25); 1 credit per delivered event, 100 per management op

streaming.name: Solana public WS logsSubscribe (pump.fun program)
streaming.status: VERIFIED (server-side only; a browser Origin gets 403)
streaming.event_shape:
Ack: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":<subId int>,"id":1}. Notification: {jsonrpc, method:'logsNotification', params {subscription, result {context {slot}, value {signature, err (null | {InstructionError:[ix,{Custom:n}]}), logs: string[] (~5-80 lines)}}}}. No balances or accounts. pump.fun Anchor events appear in logs as 'Program data: <base64>'.
TradeEvent (discriminator bddb7fd34ee661ee = 'vdt/007mYe...'), decoded and verified against balance deltas: mint pubkey, sol_amount u64 (lamports, excludes fees), token_amount u64 (raw, 6 decimals), is_buy bool, user pubkey, timestamp i64 (s), virtual_sol_reserves, virtual_token_reserves, real_sol_reserves, real_token_reserves (u64), fee_recipient pubkey, fee_basis_points u64 (95), fee u64, creator pubkey, creator_fee_basis_points u64 (30), creator_fee u64, track_volume bool, total_unclaimed_tokens, total_claimed_tokens, current_sol_volume u64, last_update_timestamp i64, ix_name string ('buy'|'buy_exact_sol_in'|'sell'), plus 109 trailing bytes of newer fields (use pump's current IDL).
Creates show 'Instruction: CreateV2' plus a CreateEvent 'Program data: G3KpTd7rY3...' (name/symbol/uri/mint...). Instruction names seen: Buy, BuyV2, BuyExactSolIn, Sell, SellV2, DistributeCreatorFees, and routers (RouteV2, SwapV2, Forward).
streaming.notes: Measured over 15-20 s: 240-260 notifications/s (only 57-73/s successful; about 70% are failed bot txs), 1.87 KB average, 0.46 MB/s. Connection opened in 220-385 ms. Headers: x-ratelimit-pubsub-limit: 10, conn-limit 40. Long txs can have truncated logs ('Log truncated'), so a TradeEvent can be missing; fall back to getTransaction. Cannot live in a Vercel function (no persistent process).

streaming.name: Solana public WS accountSubscribe
streaming.event_shape: {jsonrpc, method:'accountNotification', params {subscription, result {context {slot}, value {lamports, owner, executable, rentEpoch, space, data {program:'spl-token', space, parsed {type:'account', info {isNative, mint, owner, state, tokenAmount {amount, decimals, uiAmount, uiAmountString}, rentExemptReserve {amount:'1488440', ...}}}}}}}}. For a bonding curve use encoding base64 and decode the reserves. That gives live price and progress per token with no tx fetch.
streaming.notes: The hot WSOL fee account gave about 3 updates/s. Sub id is a large int (e.g. 52552508). A per-token accountSubscribe on bonding curves/pool vaults is the cheapest live-price feed.

streaming.name: publicnode WS (keyless, browser-capable)
streaming.event_shape: standard Solana notifications (identical shapes to above)
streaming.notes: Delivered only about 69-111 logs/s vs 240-260/s on the official WS in the same window, and 0-0.1 vs 3 account updates/s, so it appears to drop or sample messages. Use only as a best-effort browser fallback; never as the source of truth for trade feeds.

streaming.name: Helius LaserStream WebSocket (standard methods)
streaming.subscribe_message: standard: accountSubscribe, programSubscribe, logsSubscribe, signatureSubscribe, slotSubscribe, blockSubscribe, ...
streaming.notes: Free: 5 concurrent connections per PROJECT (across keys), 1,000 subscriptions per connection; Dev 150, Biz 250, Pro 1,000. Metered at 2 credits per 0.1 MB plus 1 credit per connection. The pump.fun logs firehose is about 33k credits/hour. 10-minute inactivity timeout; ping every 30-60 s. About 200 ms faster than Agave WS.

streaming.name: Helius transactionSubscribe (Helius extension)
streaming.event_shape: {method:'transactionNotification', params {subscription, result {transaction {transaction ([base64,'base64'] or jsonParsed), meta {err, status, fee, preBalances, postBalances, innerInstructions, logMessages, preTokenBalances, postTokenBalances, rewards, loadedAddresses, computeUnitsConsumed}}, signature, slot, transactionIndex}}}. The same swap derivation applies directly; no getTransaction round-trip.
streaming.notes: Up to 50,000 addresses in include/exclude/required. failed:false removes about 70% of pump noise. maxSupportedTransactionVersion is required for accounts/full details.

streaming.name: Helius Parsed Streams (parsedTransactionSubscribe)
streaming.status: DOCUMENTED (all plans incl. Free; 1 credit per delivered event)
streaming.subscribe_message: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"parsedTransactionSubscribe","params":[{"programs":["6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P"],"instructionNames":["create_v2","migrate"],"accounts":{"include":[],"roles":{}}},{"commitment":"confirmed","details":"full"|"matched"|"raw"}]}. Use describeProgram {program:<id>} to get exact instruction names first.
streaming.event_shape: {method:'parsedTransactionNotification', params {subscription, result {... transaction context (fee lamports, accountKeys incl. ALT keys), nativeTransfers[], tokenTransfers[], summary {type, description, parsedData}, instructions[] {instructionIndex, innerInstructionIndex, stackHeight, programId, programName, instructionName, decoded {args, accounts[]}}, matchedIndexes[]}}}
streaming.notes: Free: 5 connections × 25 subscriptions per project. At 1 credit per event, good for Pulse New Pairs (pump creates) and Migrated (migrate/complete events). Too expensive for all pump trades (about 60 successful/s, roughly 5M events/day).

streaming.name: Helius LaserStream gRPC
streaming.status: DOCUMENTED (mainnet needs Business $499+; devnet on Developer)
streaming.subscribe_message: Yellowstone-compatible SubscribeRequest (transactions/accounts/slots filters, up to 48 h replay)
streaming.notes: Needs a persistent backend process, so it is not usable on Vercel serverless. 2 credits per 0.1 MB.

streaming.name: Helius Webhooks (push to Vercel)
streaming.event_shape: raw: array of getTransaction-like objects; enhanced: EnhancedTransaction[]
streaming.auth: authHeader echoed in the Authorization header
streaming.notes: The only Helius real-time product that fits Vercel's no-persistent-process model. Store in a DB/KV and push to browsers via polling or SSE.

orbyt_fit: Discover (token table): Helius DAS getAssetBatch gives metadata for up to 1,000 mints per call. Supply comes from getTokenSupply, or from getMultipleAccounts jsonParsed on Token-2022 mints, which returns name/symbol/uri on-chain. Do NOT use DAS price_info for live prices (≤600 s cache, verified tokens only). Prices and volume should come from DEX/pool data providers or bonding-curve reserves.

Pulse New Pairs: Helius Parsed Streams parsedTransactionSubscribe filtered on the pump.fun program and instruction create_v2 costs 1 credit per event. Alternatively a server-side logsSubscribe(mentions pump.fun) that watches for 'Instruction: CreateV2' and the CreateEvent 'Program data'. Metadata is on-chain in the Token-2022 tokenMetadata extension.

Pulse Final Stretch: batch getMultipleAccounts (≤100 bonding curves per call, 1 Helius credit) and decode real_token_reserves. Progress = 1 − real_token_reserves/793.1M. Live per-token updates via accountSubscribe (base64) on the bonding-curve PDA.
Pulse Migrated: Parsed Streams on the pump program for the migrate instruction, or bonding curve complete=true plus PumpSwap pool creation (Enhanced type CREATE_POOL, source PUMP_AMM).

Price / market cap for bonding-curve tokens: from the curve account or the TradeEvent virtual reserves, price in SOL = (vSol/1e9)/(vTok/1e6) and mcap = price × 1e9 supply, then multiply by a SOL/USD quote. Real, on-chain, no third party.

Trades feed (token page): Helius transactionSubscribe accountInclude=[bondingCurve or pool], failed:false, jsonParsed, maxSupportedTransactionVersion:1 (Developer plan), then apply the swap derivation. On Free: poll getSignaturesForAddress(pool, limit 20..50) plus getTransaction via a Vercel route with short cache, or Parsed Events transaction-history (10 credits per page of up to 100 parsed txs). The pump.fun TradeEvent in logs gives exact sol/token amounts, trader, and post-trade reserves.

Chart / candles: the only way from raw RPC is to backfill trades (getTransactionsForAddress on the pool, full, asc, 1,000 per call, 10 credits per 100 txs) and aggregate OHLCV yourself. Prefer a dedicated OHLCV provider for charts and use RPC only to append live ticks.

Holders: Helius DAS getTokenAccounts({mint}) with full pagination (1,000 per page, 10 credits per page) for counts and distribution; getTokenLargestAccounts (Helius only; the public RPC blocks it) for the top 20. Resolve account to owner and exclude curve/pool vaults.

Wallet tracker: Helius webhooks (raw, up to 100k addresses per webhook, 1 credit per event) posting to a Vercel route and then a store. On Developer+, transactionSubscribe with accountInclude and tokenAccounts:'balanceChanged'. Label swaps via the derivation or Parsed Events.

Wallet analytics / PnL: getTransactionsForAddress(wallet, transactionDetails:'full', filters.status:'succeeded', filters.tokenAccounts:'balanceChanged', sortOrder:'asc', encoding:'jsonParsed', maxSupportedTransactionVersion:1) gives complete fills. Derive per-mint cost basis in SOL from the balance deltas. Parsed Events history gives human-readable labels.

Portfolio: Helius getAssetsByOwner(showFungible, showNativeBalance) in one call (10 credits); raw fallback getBalance + getTokenAccountsByOwner × 2 programs (Tokenkeg and Token-2022), filtering zero balances.

Risk: getMultipleAccounts jsonParsed on the mint gives mintAuthority/freezeAuthority (both null for pump.fun), Token-2022 extensions (transfer fee, permanent delegate, etc. via DAS mint_extensions), plus top-holder concentration from getTokenLargestAccounts.
Quotes / trading (not tested): Helius Sender (0 credits plus a tip) and the Priority Fee API (1 credit) are available. Tx building is outside RPC-read scope.
gotchas: TRANSACTION V1 IS LIVE (SIMD-0385, mainnet since 2026-09-15). getTransaction without maxSupportedTransactionVersion:1 fails with -32015 'Transaction version (1) is not supported by the requesting client'. I hit this on 2 of the pump.fun trades I sampled. getBlock fails entirely if ANY tx in the block is v1. v1 messages carry transactionConfig {computeUnitLimit, heapSize, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit, priorityFee (total lamports)} and no ComputeBudget instructions or ALTs (max 64 accounts). SDKs need @solana/kit ≥ 8.0 or @solana/web3.js v3; legacy web3.js 1.x cannot deserialize v1. Raw fetch with jsonParsed avoids this.

api.mainnet-beta.solana.com (and api.mainnet.solana.com) return HTTP 403 'Access forbidden' to ANY request with an Origin header, which covers every browser fetch and WebSocket. The CORS preflight succeeds, which is misleading. Server/proxy only.

Public RPC per-method limits are per IP per 10 s: getTransaction, getSignaturesForAddress and getTokenAccountsByOwner = 10; getMultipleAccounts = 50; getBalance and getTokenSupply = 150. getTokenLargestAccounts has method-limit 0, so it always returns 429 with retry-after 10. Vercel's shared egress IPs make this worse. It is unusable for a trade feed at about 60 pump trades/s.

publicnode is browser-friendly but blocks indexed methods (getTokenSupply, getTokenAccountsByOwner, getProgramAccounts need a personal token; getTokenLargestAccounts blocked) and its WS delivered only about 40% of the official stream's notifications.
getSignaturesForAddress and logsSubscribe include FAILED txs: about 70% of pump.fun-mentioning txs fail (bot spam), and the latest 5 program signatures were all failed. Filter err===null.

logsSubscribe 'mentions' takes exactly one address. There is no balance data in logs notifications. Decode the pump.fun TradeEvent from 'Program data:' (discriminator bddb7fd34ee661ee; layout in the streaming notes) or fetch the tx. Logs can be truncated on big txs.

Instruction names are unreliable for trade direction: PumpSwap 'BuyExactQuoteIn' on an inverted pool was actually the user SELLING the token for SOL. Always derive side from the trader's balance deltas.

The trader is not always accountKeys[0]: a relayer/fee-payer pattern was seen live (aggregator DF1ow...). Pick the signer whose token balances changed. For pump.fun, the TradeEvent 'user' field is authoritative.
WSOL wrap/unwrap accounts created and closed within one tx never appear in pre/postTokenBalances. The SOL leg shows only in pre/postBalances of the signer, so add meta.fee back and exclude ATA rent.

Rent was reduced: getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(165) = 1,488,440 lamports (was 2,039,280). A 170-byte Token-2022 ATA holds 1,513,840, but some txs still over-fund with 2,039,280. Never hardcode rent; compute it from account lamport deltas.

Wallet net SOL includes third-party bot/router fees and tips. The v1 sell fixture lost about 0.02 SOL to a FLASHX bot fee plus a 100,000-lamport tip. For 'trade price' use pool-side deltas or TradeEvent sol_amount (which excludes pump's 0.95% protocol fee and 0.30% creator fee); for 'wallet PnL' use wallet deltas.

Amounts: uiTokenAmount.amount and supply are raw strings that can exceed 2^53 (BONK supply 8.8e18), so use BigInt. uiAmount floats are lossy. rentEpoch = 18446744073709552000 (u64 max, lossy in JS). blockTime and TradeEvent timestamp are UNIX SECONDS. Balances are in lamports (1e9 per SOL). pump.fun tokens have 6 decimals and 1e9 supply (1e15 raw).

pump.fun tokens are now Token-2022 (mint suffix 'pump', owner TokenzQd...), created via CreateV2 with metadataPointer and tokenMetadata extensions. Always query both token programs. Some PumpSwap mints are not 'pump'-suffixed (e.g. 5RJGBa...).

pump.fun bonding-curve config is not constant: initial virtual SOL differed between curves (about 30 SOL vs about 0.45 SOL), while virtual minus real token offset was 279.9M on both. Compute price from actual reserves and don't assume the classic constants.

getTokenAccountsByOwner returns zero-balance accounts (18 Token-2022 accounts, mostly 0, on the tested wallet). getTokenLargestAccounts and DAS getTokenAccounts return TOKEN ACCOUNTS; resolve owners and exclude curve/pool vaults. The DAS getTokenAccounts 'total' is the count in the current page only.

Helius Enhanced Transactions (/v0/transactions, /v0/addresses/{a}/transactions) are LEGACY/maintenance mode at 100 credits per call with no new parsers. Its tokenTransfers[].tokenAmount is DECIMAL-ADJUSTED, while events.swap and accountData use rawTokenAmount {tokenAmount (raw string), decimals}. PUMP_AMM trades are typed BUY/SELL (not SWAP), so type=SWAP filters miss them. History pagination param is 'before-signature' (not 'before'), limit 1-100 (default 10), and a type filter can return a 'Failed to find events within the search period ... before-signature <sig>' continuation error.

Helius Parsed Events (the successor, 10 credits) uses rawTokenAmount (raw) plus decimals, lowercase summary.type ('swap'), snake_case decoded args with u64 as strings, per-item parserStatus, no server-side type filter, and 'processed' is unsupported. Metering started 2026-09-24.

Helius WebSocket data is metered (2 credits per 0.1 MB plus 1 per connection) and Free allows only 5 concurrent WSS connections per project across ALL its keys. Giving each browser user a Helius WS will exhaust connections and credits. Fan out from one consumer, or use webhooks plus polling.

Helius Allowed-Domains rules rely on browser Origin/Referer and are spoofable by scripts: they limit casual key theft, not abuse. Use a separate low-budget key for any NEXT_PUBLIC_ URL. Allowed IPs don't suit Vercel (dynamic egress) unless you pay for static IPs. The Secure URL (5 req/s per IP) is paid-only, and whether it supports WSS is UNCERTAIN.

Helius getTransactionsForAddress and getTransfersByAddress cannot be JSON-RPC-batched. getTransfersByAddress is Developer+ only (Free gets an error). DAS price_info is cached ≤600 s and exists only for verified tokens.
Vercel serverless cannot keep WebSockets or gRPC (LaserStream) open. Server-side streaming needs an external always-on worker; webhooks are the serverless-native push option.
terms_and_risks:
Solana public RPC: Solana's docs say the endpoints are "not intended for production applications" and that high-traffic websites may be blocked without prior notice. On top of that, browser Origins are already hard-blocked (403) and getTokenLargestAccounts is disabled. Treat it as a dev-only or last-resort server fallback.

publicnode (Allnodes): a free community endpoint with no SLA. Throttling is opaque, indexed methods require a personal token, and the WS appears to drop messages. Not suitable as a source of truth for "real data".

Helius: commercial ToS. Free plan quotas are tight: 1M credits, 10 rps, 5 WS connections. Keys exposed in the browser can be abused and drain credits; autoscaling is on by default only for Business/Pro, and Free simply stops.
- Enhanced Transactions is deprecated (maintenance mode, 100 credits) and may be sunset; build on Parsed Events or your own jsonParsed derivation instead.
- Parsed Events and Parsed Streams have been billed since 2026-09-24 (not charged until 2026-10-01 for prior users). Gatekeeper beta.helius-rpc.com is labelled beta but serves the same APIs.
- The Wallet API is beta, and its prices are hourly estimates (unsuitable for "real-time" displays).
- DAS prices are cached up to 10 min.

Data integrity: every figure here derives from on-chain state or txs, but net figures include third-party fees and tips, and failed txs must be excluded. Displayed prices should state their source (curve reserves vs trade price vs cached DAS).

Artifacts: 22 genuine response fixtures in tests/fixtures/rpc-helius/. Helper scripts are in .../research/tmp/rpc-helius/: derive.mjs (swap derivation), decode.cjs (pump TradeEvent decoder), ws.mjs, wsbytes.mjs, burst.mjs. Helius docs and OpenAPI copies are in .../tmp/rpc-helius/hdocs/.
